raw_response:
I farm 57 mu, so I cannot do things too loosely, but I also do not gamble. I have done this many years. What worked on my land, I keep; what costs too much, I hold back. This year I will still keep most land in maize because it is steady and easier to manage on bigger area. Stevia brings cash if the stand is good, but it needs more watching, more labor, and cleaner fields, so I will not put all the land into it.

For maize, I will plant after the soil warms up, around late April to early May. I will use the hybrid seed people around here commonly buy, not the most expensive one, just the one with decent ears and stable yield. I usually put manure or base fertilizer first, then some urea later when the crop is growing strong. If I see drought, I will irrigate from the well, but I do not want to pump too many times because electricity and water cost money. For stevia, I will keep a smaller area because it is a cash crop but needs more hands. I will make sure the land is fine and clean before planting, use bought seedlings, give fertilizer in a few rounds, irrigate when it is dry, and watch weeds and insects more carefully than maize. I would rather do a little less area well than spread myself too thin.
